directAnswer: St. John I was pope from 523 to 526 and the first pope known to have traveled to Constantinople. King Theodoric sent him there to ask Emperor Justin I to ease measures against Arians, and on his return Theodoric, suspecting him of conspiring with the emperor, had him detained at Ravenna, where he died. The Church honors him as a martyr on May 18.

paras: John, born in Tuscany, was an elderly deacon when elected in August 523. Italy was ruled by Theodoric the Ostrogoth, an Arian who had long tolerated the Catholic majority. By the 520s, however, relations between Theodoric and the Roman senatorial class were deteriorating.

Theodoric suspected that leading Romans favored the Eastern emperor. He imprisoned and executed the senator and philosopher Boethius, author of The Consolation of Philosophy, and later Boethius's father-in-law Symmachus.

Emperor Justin I had begun to act against Arians in the East, closing their churches. Theodoric, himself an Arian, demanded that the pope go to Constantinople to seek relief for his coreligionists. John, accompanied by several bishops and senators, left in late 525.

In Constantinople he was received with great honor. He celebrated Easter in the city's principal church, and the Liber Pontificalis says the emperor was crowned by him, a detail historians treat cautiously. Justin agreed to return churches to the Arians but would not allow those who had converted to Catholicism to return to Arianism, which had been one of Theodoric's demands.

When John returned in 526, Theodoric regarded the warm reception in Constantinople and the partial results with suspicion. He detained the pope at Ravenna, where John died on May 18, 526, worn down by confinement and ill treatment.

His body was brought to Rome and buried in St. Peter's, and he was soon venerated as a martyr. Theodoric himself died a few months later. During John's reign, the monk Dionysius Exiguus completed his Easter tables, which counted years from the Incarnation and gave rise to the Anno Domini dating system.

keyFacts: Pope from 523 to 526; born in Tuscany
First pope known to have visited Constantinople (525–526)
Sent by King Theodoric to seek relief for Arians from Emperor Justin I
Died in detention at Ravenna in May 526; venerated as a martyr
Buried at St. Peter's; feast day May 18

faqs.question: Why did Theodoric imprison Pope John I?
faqs.answer: Theodoric suspected that John had grown too close to Emperor Justin I during his embassy to Constantinople and had not obtained everything the king demanded. He detained the pope in Ravenna, where John died.

faqs.question: Was Pope John I a martyr?
faqs.answer: He is venerated as a martyr because he died from harsh treatment while held by Theodoric. He was not executed, but his death was seen as a consequence of his fidelity.

faqs.question: What did Pope John I achieve in Constantinople?
faqs.answer: He was honored by Emperor Justin I and celebrated Easter there. Justin agreed to restore churches to Arians but refused to let converts return to Arianism.
